 ----Respondents For Appellant(s) : Mr. Mudit Vaishnav for Mr. Rajesh  Panwar, Sr. Advocate For Respondent(s) : Mr. LD Khatri
Mr. Jairam Saran  HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE NUPUR BHATI Order 11/09/2024 1.
Heard.
Perused the material available on record.

2. By way of the instant misc. appeal filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('the Act of 1988'), the appellant/claimant has sought enhancement of the compensation and has sought modification of the judgment & award dated 17.12.2007 passed by the learned Judge MACT, Pali in Nasir Mohd.@ Nasir Ahmed vs Mahendra Singh And Anr. ...

1

MACT Case [2024:RJ-JD:37830] (2 of 5) [CMA-922/2009] No.79/2006 whereby the learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim of the claimants by awarding an amount to the tune of Rs.11,40,000/- @ 7% p.a. in their favour.

3. Succinctly stated facts of the case are that on 22.09.2005, at around 8:30 am, Nasir Mohammad and Mahendra Singh were going Bikaner on a maruti car, when they reached near Barani Village,
the respondent No.1 driving the truck bearing No.RJ-19- G-7001 in a rash and negligent manner, hit the maruti car and due to which, Nasir Mohammad received grievous injuries one person namely Mahendra Singh succumbed to death.
4. Learned Tribunal has issued the notices.
Despite being served the notice, none appeared for respondent No.1 and therefore, ex-parte proceedings was initiated against him.
The respondent No.2-Insurance Company in its reply denied all averments made in the claim petition.
5. In support of their claim petition, the appellants-claimants produced 6 witnesses and exhibited documents to prove their case.
Oral as well as documentary evidence were also produced to prove the case.
No evidence was produced in defence.

As per pleadings, issues were framed by the learned Tribunal and after hearing both the parties, the learned Tribunal passed the award in favour of the appellants/claimants and being dissatisfied from the award, the appellants have preferred the instant misc. appeal.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that the learned Tribunal has seriously erred in awarding meager compensation and therefore, the award deserves to be modified and the compensation deserves to be enhanced.

He further submits that at the time of accident, the claimant was aged 48 [2024:RJ-JD:37830] (3 of 5) [CMA-922/2009] years however, the learned Tribunal had erred in considering the age of claimant to be 52 years.

It is also submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that the injuries sustained by him in that accident is serious in nature which resulted into 90% permanent disability and the nature of job in which the claimant was engaged, the said disability resulted into 100% loss of income.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the claimant/ appellant was not awarded under the head 'Future Prospects' as per the report of ITR, the appellant was 48 years of age at the time of incident and he has become virtually incapable of doing anything on account of the injuries cause to him.
He further submits that the learned Tribunal seriously erred in not awarding any compensation under the pain and suffering, thus under this head, amount should be awarded.

He also submits that the award passed by the learned Tribunal towards loss of income suffered during the medical treatment, is slightly on a lower side and thus, the same needs to be enhanced.
8.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company vehemently opposes the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the claimant/appellant and submits that the learned Tribunal has rightly passed the award and the same does not call for any interference.

He further submits that inasmuch as this is a matter wherein the claimant has suffered injuries, the future prospects, towards loss of income has rightly not been considered by the learned Tribunal while awarding compensation.

sentences.text: 2 9 . I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submissions advanced at Bar and have gone through the material available on record.

Thus, looking to the factual matrix of the case and applying the ratio of the judgment rendered by Hon'ble the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi &
Ors. : 2017 16 SCC 680, Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation : AIR 2009 SC 3104 along with Pappu Deo Yadav Vs. Naresh Kumar : AIR 2020 SC4424, the instant misc. appeal is partly allowed and the award passed by the learned MACT, Pali in MACT Case No.79/2006 stands modified to the extent of awarding Future Prospect for loss of income, compensation towards pain and suffering and medical bills as produced by the claimant.

sentences.text: Both the counsel are directed to submit the calculation.

The compensation is enhanced in the following manner:-
Yearly Income assessed by the Tribunal Rs.60,000/- Applying future prospects @
25% i.e. Rs.75,000/- 60,000+25% of 60,000 Applying the multiply on the said income and Rs. 8,77,500/-
taking into consideration 90% permanent disability suffered by the claimant (75,000X13X90%)

(A)
(Add) Medical Bills (B) Rs.9,85,425/-
(Add) Traveling expenses (C) Rs.20,000/-
(Add) Attendant charges as awarded by Rs.65,000/-
Tribunal Pain and suffering (17.50% of the total award Rs.1,68,437.50/-
excluding medical bills), i.e. (E)
TOTAL (A+B+C+D+E) Rs.21,16,362.50/-
Amount awarded by the learned Tribunal Rs.11,40,000/-
Enhanced amount Rs.9,76,361.50/-
11. The insurance company is directed to pay the enhanced compensation of Rs.9,76,361.50/- along with interest @ 6% p.a. to the claimant within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this award, failing the claimant shall be [2024:RJ-JD:37830] (5 of 5) [CMA-922/2009] entitled to receive interest @
7.5% per annum on the enhanced compensation.
12. The amount, if any, already paid by the respondent- Insurance Company, shall be adjusted towards the amount finally awarded by this Court.
13. No order as to costs.
